target_customer: Robot makers and operators (warehouses, grocery stores, data centers) who need manipulation models
problem: Robot hardware is converging but manipulation intelligence is the bottleneck. The company trains models on human demonstrations captured with custom gloves in data factories and retargets them to different robots.
business_model: Foundation models for manipulation sold or deployed to robot operators; pricing not found
product_category: Robot manipulation foundation models and human demonstration data

founders.name: Jalaj Shukla
education: University of Pennsylvania, MS robotics and mechatronics
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page; GRASP Lab research assistant.

competitors.name: MANUS (data gloves) and its customers such as Mimic Robotics
competitors.what: Motion capture gloves used by robotics teams to collect human hand demonstration data
competitors.traction_then: named by NVIDIA as official data glove for Isaac Teleop at GTC 2026 (vendor and press claims)

competitors.name: Sunday Robotics skill capture glove
competitors.what: Glove that records operators doing real manipulation for training data
competitors.traction_then: listed on backorder in a third-party listing

technical_complexity.rationale: Cross-embodiment manipulation policies trained from human gloved demonstrations and retargeted to many hands is research-grade work, plus custom sensing hardware and data operations.

defensibility.rationale: Data collection with off-the-shelf or custom gloves is widely copied, and well-funded labs pursue the same approach. A proprietary demonstration dataset could compound but is unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known; no sourced incumbent action against this company.

market_need_then: Humanoid and dexterous robot hardware investment grew through 2025 and 2026 and teams reported a data bottleneck for dexterous hands (ICRA 2026 coverage by a glove vendor, so a vendor view).

branding.domain_note: Uses intelligence-factory.com, an exact .com with a hyphen.

identity.voice_and_tone: Bold and mission driven with sweeping claims and short slogans ('Human Intelligence for Robots')

branding.brand_signature: Human Intelligence for Robots; the 'data factory' framing

brand_strength.rationale: Clear tagline but a generic name that is easy to confuse with other 'intelligence factory' phrases, and no independent brand press.

outcome_analysis: Intelligence Factory is a Spring 2026 company with about ten people according to YC and strong robotics founders. It has no verified funding or revenue, so its outcome is open. The main questions are whether its glove-collected human data beats rivals and whether customers beyond early warehouse and data center pilots appear.
notes: Unverified funding: aggregators list a $500K pre-seed in June 2026 with Y Combinator, and PitchBook lists Auxilium Partners and Enzo Ventures; one profile says the company is not funded. No primary source, so no round recorded. Team size conflicts (YC page 10, search listings 5 or 6). No GTM or customer names found. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed (16 June 2026, FundedIQ) is now recorded and rests on aggregators only. PitchBook names Auxilium Partners and Enzo Ventures among investors but does not tie them to this round, so they are left out.
